items.title: Meta Ads: $45.73 spend, 1 lead, $45.73 CPL — Flooring Problems Campaign
items.summary: Yesterday (2026-08-14) Meta spent $45.73 across the only actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 1 lead at $45.73 CPL. That's roughly 2.9x the 7-day baseline CPL (~$15.67 over $344.83 / 22 leads), but yesterday's window spend was below the $50 minimum spend floor for flagging a CPL anomaly, so no anomaly item is raised. Account is ACTIVE and no ads are flagged.

needs_attention: Flooring Problems Campaign's CPL yesterday ($45.73) ran ~2.9x the 7-day baseline ($15.67) on just 1 lead from $45.73 spend — below the $50 window-spend floor the anomaly rule requires before flagging, so this is reported for context only, not as an anomaly item. Worth a glance if the low lead count continues.

Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again include lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads, offsite_search_add_meta_leads, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads — each valued at 1 yesterday, matching the counted leads exactly, same as prior runs). Still no discrepancy, but per the agent's trap note this should be reviewed for whether the script's lead-action set needs extending, not hand-patched here.
